libraries.page.title: Libraries
libraries.page.lede: What Studio needs on the machine that runs it: the training environment, Instant NuRec, CUDA renderers, the SDK for each dataset, tools. Installable items have a button (pip into the Python running Studio, or the steps of envs/install_main.sh, envs/install_nurec.sh, envs/install_xsim.sh); one install at a time, with progress and log at the top. Reopen Studio afterwards to load new packages.
libraries.all.help: Installs every missing item in turn (main environment, Instant NuRec, dataset SDKs, tools) without changing installed package versions. Skips Waymo and nuPlan (they may change the main environment's packages) and manual items; items this machine cannot install (no GPU, not Linux, no Rust) are skipped with the reason.
libraries.all.confirm: Install {count} missing items: {names}? The main environment and NuRec can take an hour.
libraries.confirm: Install {name} on the Studio machine? About {size}, {minutes} minutes.
nav.activity.title: Activity
palette.placeholder: Type a scene, run or page…
activity.runs.title: Running and queued runs on this machine
activity.remote.title: Kaggle, Colab runs not pulled yet
activity.remote.hint: They may be queued, running, finished, or not pushed yet. Open the run, Kaggle (Colab) tab, to see the real status and pull the results.
activity.jobs.title: Background jobs
activity.jobs.none: No background jobs since Studio started.
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.info: Ask about scenes, approaches, presets, where to run, run errors. Questions are sent with Studio's current facts (scenes, splits, approaches, recent runs, environment, GPUs; no API keys) to the provider you choose. When the assistant proposes a setup you get a button that opens New run with it; you still review before starting.
assistant.key_keep: leave empty to keep the saved key
assistant.privacy: The key is stored on the Studio machine (~/.config/drive2sim/assistant.json, readable only by its owner) and is never shown again in the browser.
assistant.placeholder: For example: which approach should this scene use on Colab?
assistant.empty: Ask something about your scenes, approaches or runs. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
overview.page.title: Overview
overview.page.lede: What is running, which results lead, and recent runs.
overview.active.title: Running now
overview.leaders.title: Leaders by Avg
overview.recent.title: Recent runs
scenes.page.title: Scenes
scenes.page.lede: Each scene is one continuous driving clip taken from a dataset (for example nuScenes scene-0061, about 20 seconds), converted to the standard format. Open a scene to see every camera, its splits and the validation report.
scenes.empty.title: No scenes yet
scenes.empty.text: Add a scene from a raw dataset folder: nuScenes, Waymo, Argoverse 2, PandaSet, KITTI, nuPlan or PhysicalAI.
ingest.title: Import scene from dataset
ingest.lede: Choose a raw dataset folder on the machine running Studio (type the path or use the folder button to open a picker). The tool detects the dataset, lists versions and sequences, then converts the one you pick in the background.
upload.title: Or upload data from this computer
upload.help: Use this when Studio runs on another machine (rented GPU, lab server through port forwarding) and the data is on your computer. Files are sent in 8 MiB chunks into uploads/<name>/ of the working directory; the upload keeps running when this drawer closes, watch and stop it on the Storage page. After a dropped connection or a page reload pick the same folder and name again and press Resume, parts already there are not sent again.
upload.name: Folder name on the Studio machine
upload.paused: Stopped at {sent} / {total}; press Resume to continue from what is already there
upload.failed: Upload failed; press Resume to retry from what is already there
drive.title: Or get data from Google Drive
drive.help: Studio opens a CPU Colab session with the active Google account (Colab section), mounts Drive there and downloads the folder you pick into uploads/<name>/ of the working directory in 32 MiB parts. The first time Google asks for permission to read Drive. Pulling again with the same name skips complete files. Stop the session afterwards so it does not use compute units.
drive.stop_help: Stop the Colab session used to read Drive (gives the VM back)
drive.consent: Google needs your permission for this session to read Drive. Open the page, pick the right account, allow, then come back and press I have allowed.
drive.not_mounted: Drive is not mounted in this session; press Connect Drive.
drive.truncated: Only the first 500 entries are shown.
drive.inspecting: Detecting the dataset in this folder…
drive.not_detected: No dataset found in this folder or its near subfolders.
drive.not_supported: Detected this dataset, but scene ingest does not support it yet.
drive.sequence_help: Pulls only the files that sequence needs: calibration/, data_poses, ImageSets-rosa-6class/ (metadata Instant NuRec needs), the four data_2d_raw/<sequence>_image_0X.tar and the LiDAR data_3d_raw/<sequence>.tar (or the extracted folders). Pulling another sequence into the same uploads/ folder skips the calibration and poses already there.
drive.inspect_truncated: Large folder: only the first 600 folders were looked at, the result may be incomplete.
drive.pull_some_help: Pulls only the selected sequence and items; clear the selection to pull the whole folder.
ingest.toast.queued: Ingest started; follow it in Activity
scene.outdated.title: This scene was ingested with an older {converter} converter
scene.outdated.detail: Output version {recorded}; the current converter writes version {current}. The scene still runs; ingest it again to use the new output (for a Kaggle scene, d2s kaggle ingest creates a new notebook automatically).
scene.kaggle.title: This scene was ingested on Kaggle: images, LiDAR and masks live on Kaggle; this machine only has the manifest and the validation report, so images cannot be shown here.
scene.kaggle.detail: Ingest notebook: {kernel}. The Cameras and Checks tabs still work. Runs of this scene must use the Kaggle executor; the training notebook attaches the ingest notebook's output.
scene.tools.title: Check the data
scene.tools.help: LiDAR: LiDAR points projected onto every camera image, coloured by depth (near red, far purple, the same scale as the depth videos); points on the ego car are grey (not used for training). With a correct calibration the points sit on the edges of houses, cars and poles. Scenes with a fixed calibration per camera and KITTI-layout LiDAR (KITTI, KITTI-360) work on any frame, with a projection checked to match the loader's; other datasets (such as nuScenes) show only the frames projected in the Checks tab. 360° panorama: merges every camera of the frame into an equirectangular image around the car (centre is forward), rotation only, so near objects may break at seams; needs a fixed calibration per camera (KITTI, KITTI-360, Waymo, Argoverse 2, nuPlan). Built only while paused.
scene.tools.failed: No LiDAR overlay for this frame: for this scene only the frames projected in the Checks tab (LiDAR on images) are available.
scene.tools.panorama_caption: Panorama of the current frame: centre is the front of the car, left of the image is the car's left; black is seen by no camera.
scene.frames.keys: Left and right arrows step; space plays
scene.splits.title: Splits
scene.splits.none: No splits yet. A split is needed to run an approach.
scene.splits.every_hint: Frames {n}, {n}×2, {n}×3… are test, the rest train
scene.splits.delete_body: A split used by runs cannot be deleted; delete those runs first.
scene.delete.title: Delete scene {scene}?
scene.delete.body: Deletes the standard data, {splits} splits, cache and {runs} runs of this scene. This cannot be undone.
new.page.title: New run
new.page.lede: Pick data and an approach. Choices that do not fit the scene are struck through with the reason; the stage lane shows what runs and what comes from cache.
new.approach.experimental.hint: Wired into the tool but not yet validated: no full training and evaluation run has finished on a GPU. Runs work, but expect failures and results that are not yet comparable.
new.dynamics.boxes.hint: Cars and people are separate nodes that follow the scene's 3D boxes.
new.dynamics.time.hint: Gaussians change over time. No 3D boxes needed, but objects are not separated from the background.
new.dynamics.option.hint: Off by default; turned on by one of this approach's options.
new.dynamics.static.hint: Builds a static map; moving objects are not reconstructed separately.
new.boxes.missing.hint: This scene has no 3D boxes, and this approach needs them.
new.need.scene: No scenes yet. Import one in
new.need.split: This scene has no split. Create one in
new.options.title: Approach config
new.plan.title: Stages to run
new.plan.no_lidar: This run does not use LiDAR.
new.plan.waiting: Pick a scene, split and approach to see the plan.
runs.page.title: Runs
runs.page.lede: All runs, newest first. Hover a row to cancel, resume or delete.
runs.empty.title: No runs yet
runs.empty.text: Start the first run from New run.
run.action.export_video_help: Renders the PLY at every frame of the segment for the split's cameras (ground truth row on top, render below), at the original speed from the frame timestamps; the eval video only has the test frames of one camera.
run.action.carla_help: Builds an OpenDRIVE map along the drive, starts CARLA 1.0 and a Gaussian render server for this run, drives the ego car in CARLA and records the cameras as a video (Videos tab).
run.action.drive_help: Drive the car in CARLA with the keyboard, seeing the run's Gaussian render.
drive.title: Drive in CARLA
drive.help: The car uses CARLA physics on a map built along the run's drive. Left: the Gaussian render from the camera on the car; right: CARLA's own 3D world seen from behind the car. The further you leave the original path, the blurrier or emptier the Gaussian view, as there is no data there.
drive.no_run: Open this page from the "Drive in CARLA" button on an Instant NuRec run.
drive.other_run: A drive session for run {run} is running. Starting here stops it.
drive.objects_help: Put the scene's vehicles and people (3D boxes, as StreetGS uses) into CARLA as actors with physics and collisions. Only in the CARLA world, the Gaussian view is unchanged; no effect on scenes without boxes.
drive.settings_hint: 50% at 20 fps is smooth enough to drive. Starting CARLA the first time takes about 30 seconds; the session uses the GPU with the most free VRAM.
drive.failed: Could not start the drive session:
drive.sim_fps_help: Physics steps CARLA runs per second; the loop targets twice the chosen frame rate, lower means the machine cannot keep up.
drive.gpu_help: Load of the whole GPU from nvidia-smi, including other processes on it.
drive.keys: W/↑ throttle (hold Shift for full), S/↓ brake, A/D or ←/→ steer, Space hand brake, Q toggles reverse, R back to start.
run.action.refine_help: Keeps optimising the NuRec Gaussians on the clip's training images with gsplat, then re-scores and re-exports the PLY and videos.
run.refine.title: Refine the NuRec scene
run.refine.body: NuRec builds the scene in one pass, so renders are blurry. This step optimises the Gaussians further on the clip's training frames (fisheye cameras via 3DGUT), inserted after reconstruction; the run's scores, PLY, drive-through video and CARLA video are redone from the new PLY. The drive-through video adds about 15–20 minutes.
run.refine.strategy.mcmc: MCMC: relocate and add Gaussians (experimental, may be worse)
run.carla.title: Run the scene in CARLA
run.carla.body: Studio builds a .usdz scene from the NCore clip, starts CARLA (if not running) and a render server for the run's PLY on the GPU with the most free VRAM. Every CARLA tick is rendered from the Gaussians and written to carla.mp4 in the Videos tab. The further the ego car leaves the original trajectory, the blurrier the images.
run.carla.ego.trajectory: CARLA physics following the original trajectory
run.carla.quality_hint: Fraction of the camera's native resolution. Higher is sharper but each tick takes longer to render.
run.delete.title: Delete run {run}?
run.delete.body: Deletes the whole run folder: checkpoints, videos, logs. Shared cache is kept. This cannot be undone.
run.error.where: Details in {log}, see the Logs tab.
run.result.wait: Results appear when the eval stage finishes.
run.result.no_eval: This run has not reached the eval stage, or eval failed.
run.live.title: Progress
run.live.not_active: No process is running this run any more.
run.live.stalled_error: The log ends in an error and has had no new line for {time}. Cancel the run, then Resume to rerun this stage.
run.live.stalled_idle: No new log line for {time} while the GPUs are almost idle. Check the log; if it is stuck, Cancel then Resume.
run.config.title: Run configuration
run.metrics.hint: Metrics stream in while this page is open during training.
run.stages.title: Stages
run.videos.writing: This video is still being written (the run is rendering). Check back in a few minutes.
run.kaggle.hint: If the Kaggle session stops, pull then push again: the next attempt resumes from the previous checkpoint.
compare.page.title: Compare
compare.page.lede: Ranks finished, fully trained runs on one scene, for one split or all splits. Running, failed, cancelled or quick-test runs are left out of the tables and charts. Metric cells go from blue (worse) to orange (better).
compare.empty.title: Nothing to compare yet
compare.empty.text: Runs appear here once their eval stage is done.
compare.side.title: Side-by-side videos
compare.merge.help: Merge the two videos shown into one MP4 (H.264, labelled with the run) to download, send or put in a report. Top/bottom: both 1280 px wide; side by side: both 480 px tall; stops at the shorter video. Stored under compare/ in the working directory and reused for the same pair.
storage.page.title: Storage
storage.page.lede: Uploaded source data (add, stop, resume, delete) and shared results in the cache (masks, SMPL…) with the runs still using them. Cleaning the cache only removes results no run uses.
storage.empty.title: Cache is empty
storage.empty.text: Preparation stages (masks, SMPL…) write here on their first run.
storage.gc.title: Clean cache
viewer.page.title: 3D viewer
viewer.page.lede: View a run's reconstructed scene in four modes (preview package, static scene, video, GPU render), or drop a splat file from this machine.
viewer.drop.text: Drop .ply, .spz, .splat, .ksplat or .sog here. Files stay in the browser.
viewer.field.up_hint: Runs from this tool: Z+ (DriveStudio frame). Dropped files: read from the file when this tool exported it, otherwise guessed from the scene's shape (flat ground, buildings and trees rising); change it by hand if the scene is upside down. COLMAP 3DGS is usually Y−.
viewer.field.sh_hint: Lower it if the view stutters.
viewer.no_webgl: This browser has no WebGL2, so splats cannot be drawn.
viewer.hud.recenter_hint: Back to the opening view: the original front camera at the current frame
run.quick_hint: Quick test run with few iterations; metrics are not comparable with full runs.
new.training.info: Full: iterations from the approach ({iters}; empty means the method config, usually 30000). Quick test: train 3000 iterations to check the approach runs end to end; metrics are not comparable with full runs.
new.executor.info: This machine: runs in the Studio queue, one run at a time. Kaggle: pushes to a GPU notebook in the background; needs the kaggle command, an API token and pushed code. Colab: runs on a Google Colab GPU VM; needs the colab command signed in and pushed code.
run.machine.several: This run ran on {count} different machines (resumed elsewhere); time and FPS are not fully comparable.
compare.mixed_gpu: Runs in this table were trained on several GPU types ({gpus}). Time, VRAM and render speed depend on the hardware, so compare them only between runs on the same GPU (see the GPU column). Image quality metrics are not affected.
nav.demo.label: Demo data
nav.demo.info: Studio is running on demo (fake) data in {workdir}: numbers, images, videos and splats are synthetic, not real results. Turn it off by restarting Studio without DEMO=1 (make dev or make studio).
new.preset.info: Click a preset to fill in the approach config below. You can still change each setting; when it no longer matches any preset, the run is recorded as custom.
new.preset.default_help: The approach's default value for every setting.
kaggle.setup.no_key: missing; click API key to enter one
kaggle.setup.source.oauth: signed in with kaggle auth login
kaggle.setup.config_dir: Kaggle CLI config folder: {dir}. A key entered here is saved in this folder (readable by the owner only) and shared with the kaggle command.
kaggle.setup.dirty: This machine has uncommitted changes. The Kaggle notebook clones the pushed commit, so these changes are not on Kaggle. Commit and push first if the run needs them.
kaggle.setup.token_help: Create one under Settings, API on Kaggle: new tokens start with KGAT_. A legacy key (32 characters in kaggle.json) also needs your username. The key is only sent to Studio on this machine and is never shown again.
kaggle.setup.start_warning: Kaggle is not ready: see the red lines above. Starting now will fail when pushing to Kaggle.
run.stages.original_hint: Reused from the cache; this is the run time of the original run that produced it.
artifacts.open_failed: Could not open the file manager
artifacts.cache_hint: Cached stages keep their results in the workdir's cache/, shared by every run on the same scene with the same parameters; deleting a run keeps them (clean up on the Storage page).
artifacts.none: This stage has no results yet.
artifacts.layout: Each run lives in runs/<scene>/<approach>/<run_id>/; tool files in d2s/, each stage's results in d2s/stages/<stage>/. Runs made on Kaggle land in the same place after pulling their results.
metrics.group.quality_hint: Rendered images compared with real camera images on the held-out test frames. Higher PSNR and SSIM, lower LPIPS are better. How it is measured: right after training (end of train.py) the model re-renders every test image (frames held out by the split, never trained on); renders are rounded to 8 bits like the source images, compared with the real camera image one by one and averaged; the eval.standard stage reads the result.
metrics.group.region_hint: PSNR over one image region only. People and vehicles cover few pixels, so whole-image PSNR hides their quality; they are the hardest part of a driving scene. How it is measured: right after training (end of train.py) the model re-renders every test image (frames held out by the split, never trained on); renders are rounded to 8 bits like the source images, compared with the real camera image one by one and averaged; the eval.standard stage reads the result.
metrics.group.time_hint: Real training time, total time from data preparation to scene.ply, and iterations trained.
metrics.group.resources_hint: Peak training VRAM, model render speed, and the GPU used. Only comparable between runs on the same GPU.
metrics.group.data_hint: Images used for training and for measuring quality, from the run's split. Runs are only comparable with the same split and the same training image size.
metrics.hint.train_resolution: Image size used for training and for PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS. DriveStudio configs downscale images when loading (downscale_when_loading), e.g. nuScenes 1600×900 to 800×450: the model only learns detail at this size.
metrics.hint.source_resolution: The cameras' original image size in the dataset (scene manifest), before downscaling.
metrics.hint.train_images: Number of images (one frame of one camera) the model learns from, per the split. E.g. nuScenes split front3: 191 frames × 3 cameras = 573 images, minus 57 test images leaves 516.
metrics.hint.test_images: Images held out from training; PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS are averaged over them.
metrics.hint.test_every: How test images are picked: 1 / N means every N-th frame is a test frame, with all its cameras (split every_nth_frame:N; DriveStudio test_image_stride=N). E.g. 1 / 10: frames 10, 20, 30… are test.
metrics.group.size_hint: A 3D scene is built from many Gaussians, each a small coloured blob in space. More Gaussians give more detail but heavier files and slower rendering. After training the model is saved in three forms for three jobs, hence three numbers: the full model (used for evaluation), the PLY file (static scene for other tools) and the preview package (viewed on the 3D viewer page, with cars moving over time).
compare.chart.pareto_hint: Each dot is a run. Runs ringed in yellow and joined by the dashed line are on the Pareto front: no other run has both higher PSNR and a better horizontal value. Runs below it have a better alternative on both counts.
compare.chart.regions_hint: Each group of bars is a run: whole image, people, vehicles, moving objects. Shows which approach reconstructs people and vehicles well, which whole-image PSNR hides.
compare.chart.breakdown_hint: Time per stage group from data preparation to scene.ply. Faded parts were reused from the cache (counted at the original run time).
compare.chart.curves_hint: Training curves of up to 6 runs, read from metrics.json. Shows which run converges faster, and whether a 3000-step quick test already shows the trend. This PSNR is measured on training images, so it is higher than test PSNR.
metrics.group.summary_hint: The main metric of each group below. Ranked by Avg (PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS combined) by default; click another column header to sort by it, every table follows.
metrics.hint.avg: Mip-NeRF's combined score: geometric mean of 10^(−PSNR/10), √(1 − SSIM) and LPIPS, three quantities expressed as errors. Lower is better. No weights, and a run's score does not change when other runs are added. Computed from the three metrics next to it, so measured at the same time.
metrics.hint.psnr: PSNR (dB, higher is better): per-pixel colour error between the rendered and the real camera image, −10·log10(MSE), over valid pixels. Sensitive to misalignment, lenient on blur. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.ssim: SSIM (0–1, higher is better): local structural similarity (luminance, contrast, edges), skimage structural_similarity over the whole image. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.lpips: LPIPS (lower is better): perceptual difference from AlexNet features (torchmetrics); closest to human judgement, catches blur that PSNR misses. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.human: PSNR over image regions with people only (cyclists and motorcyclists included): the rectangle around each projected 3D box, objects fully inside the frame. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.vehicle: PSNR over image regions with cars, buses and trucks only: the rectangle around each projected 3D box. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.dynamic: PSNR over all moving objects (people and vehicles) together. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.occupied: PSNR over every region except the sky (sky mask from prep.masks_segformer). Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.train_time: Real training time: training steps only (data, forward, backward, update), summed over resumes; excludes start-up, checkpoint loading, preview renders, checkpoint saving and final evaluation. Measured during training, saved with each checkpoint (train_stats.json).
metrics.hint.recon_time: Total time of the stages from data preparation until scene.ply is written, from the per-stage times the engine records in run.json; cached stages count their original run time. Computed when building the table.
metrics.hint.iters: Iterations (steps) trained, read from train_stats.json written with the last checkpoint.
metrics.hint.vram: Peak VRAM of the training process (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated), the maximum over resumes. Measured during training, not evaluation.
metrics.hint.fps: Frames the model renders per second, measured while evaluating the test set right after training, on the training GPU: model render time only (the approach's renderer, every part of the model), first frames skipped. Not the 3D viewer page speed.
metrics.hint.gpu: GPU of the machine that ran the run, recorded when the run starts or resumes (env.json); several GPUs means it resumed on another machine.
metrics.hint.gaussians: Gaussians in the trained model, covering everything it reconstructs: background, cars, people, deformable objects. This is the most complete number and the model used for PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS. Counted when the final checkpoint is saved.
metrics.hint.ply_gaussians: Gaussians in scene.ply, written automatically at the end of every run by the export.ply_world stage: a single file holding the static scene, for other 3DGS viewers or tools. It holds the static background of the whole stretch driven (all frames merged). By default there are no cars; setting rigid_frame of the export.ply_world stage adds the cars, frozen at that frame. People, deformable objects, the sky and almost transparent Gaussians are always dropped, so this is smaller than the model count. The preview package's splat files are not included (they have their own column).
metrics.hint.ply_size: Size of scene.ply (one file, the static scene; see the scene.ply Gaussians column).
metrics.hint.preview_gaussians: Gaussians in the preview package (Export preview button), summed over all its splat files: the background, one file per car in actors/ and one per person in humans/ (packages 0.2 and later use .spz; old 0.1 packages use .ply and have no people). The package is viewed on the 3D viewer page: the background stays still, each car is moved and rotated per frame and people bend with their SMPL bones (not 4DGS); the sky is included; deformable objects are not yet, and almost transparent Gaussians are dropped. Empty if the run has not exported it.
metrics.hint.preview_size: Total size of all files in the preview package: background, cars, people, sky, and the per-frame car poses and human poses.
compare.side.info: Pick two runs to watch their test-set videos side by side; Play starts both videos together at the same time.
compare.charts.only_iters: The charts below only include the {count}-iteration runs; shorter probe runs are only in the table.
compare.arrows: Arrows next to metric names follow the paper convention: ↑ higher is better, ↓ lower is better. The small icon at the end of a header shows the sorted column and direction.
compare.sort.click: Click to sort by this column; click again to reverse
compare.by_split.label: Split display
compare.mixed_split: This table mixes runs from several splits ({splits}). Image quality metrics are measured on each split's test frames, so compare them only between runs of the same split (see the Split column, or group by split).
compare.chart.mixed_split: This chart mixes runs from several splits ({splits}): PSNR is measured on each split's test frames and does not compare across splits. Choose Group by split to colour and connect the Pareto front per split.
compare.chart.mixed_gpu: This chart has runs on different GPUs ({gpus}): time, VRAM and FPS depend on hardware, compare them only between runs on the same GPU.
ingest.action.pick: Choose a folder on this machine
ingest.action.picking: Waiting for a folder in the dialog…
viewer.mode.hint: Preview package: the browser draws the background, sky, cars and people, with cars and people moving per frame and a smooth free camera. When you stop for about 0.3 s and the machine running Studio can render (NVIDIA GPU and the PyTorch environment), an exact image from the model's original renderer, same as the train-stage videos, is overlaid automatically; the first time takes about 12 s to load the model. Otherwise only the browser version is shown (approximate: slightly different colours, no deformable objects yet). Static scene: the browser draws scene.ply, background only. Video: plays the MP4 videos the train stage rendered along the original cameras; everything is there but the camera is fixed. GPU render: the machine running Studio renders continuously from the checkpoint with the original renderer (DriveStudio's viewer); resolution drops while dragging.
viewer.mode.preview.sub: Smooth while moving, exact image when still
viewer.mode.preview.missing: Not exported; use Export preview on the run page
viewer.exact.loading: Loading the model for exact images…
viewer.exact.hint: When still, the image shown is the exact one from the model's original renderer (same as the train-stage videos); while dragging, it is the browser version.
viewer.mode.video.sub: Videos rendered along the original cameras
viewer.mode.gpu.sub: Complete, drawn live on this machine's GPU
viewer.mode.gpu.missing: This run has no checkpoint to render (Instant NuRec only has scene.ply)
viewer.gpu.unsupported: Instant NuRec runs have no DriveStudio checkpoint, so GPU rendering is not available: the model only infers scene.ply. View the scene with the static (PLY) or Video mode.
viewer.gpu.title: GPU render on the machine running Studio
viewer.gpu.fix.gpu: no NVIDIA GPU found (nvidia-smi does not run)
viewer.gpu.fix.pytorch: not installed in the tool's Python environment
viewer.gpu.fix.cuda: PyTorch is missing or cannot see the GPU (a CPU-only build, or the driver is too old)
viewer.gpu.fix.gsplat: gsplat-geer is not installed in the tool's Python environment
viewer.gpu.fix.checkpoint: no checkpoint_final.pth; for a Kaggle run, run d2s kaggle pull
viewer.gpu.fix.smpl_model: missing SMPL_NEUTRAL.pkl; place it in <workdir>/smpl_models/ or set D2S_SMPL_MODEL
viewer.gpu.not_ready: This machine cannot do GPU rendering yet. Fix the items marked X and check again. Meanwhile, use Video mode to see everything.
run.action.reexport_hint: The run already has this file. Re-export only if the export stage failed, the file was deleted, or the export code changed.
viewer.gpu.starting: Loading the checkpoint and scene data onto the GPU, usually a few tens of seconds…
viewer.gpu.exited: The GPU viewer stopped (code {code}). The end of its log is below.

Needs git and uv. Other models: bash envs/install_nurec.sh --models pa-front,pq-front.
new.env.install_hint_xsim: The script fetches the XSIM source at the pinned commit, builds its own Python 3.11 venv with uv (PyTorch 2.8 CUDA 12.8) and compiles pytoast and xsimgs into {file} (set D2S_XSIM_DIR to change it). Needs git and an NVIDIA GPU. The main environment is still needed for data preparation and scoring: bash envs/install_main.sh.

new.env.nurec_notebook_hint: Instant NuRec runs cannot be pushed to Kaggle or Colab like other approaches (the remote machine only installs the main environment). The notebook installs NuRec and reconstructs a scene; in the first cell set the paths on that machine to an NCore clip (the prep.ncore result folder under cache/, uploaded or through Drive) and to the checkpoint. The result is a PLY on that machine's disk; download it and drag it into the 3D page.
env.install.confirm_nurec:
Install Instant NuRec on the Studio machine?

The script fetches NVIDIA's source, builds a separate Python 3.11 venv with uv (PyTorch, nvidia-ncore; a few GB) and downloads a 0.7 GB checkpoint. The main environment is not touched.
env.install.confirm_xsim:
Install XSIM on the Studio machine?

The script fetches the XSIM source, builds a separate Python 3.11 venv with uv (PyTorch 2.8; a few GB) and compiles the CUDA extensions, which takes a while. The main environment is not touched.
env.install.confirm:
Install the {env} environment into the Python running Studio ({python})?

The script installs PyTorch and requirements.txt and builds gsplat-geer, nvdiffrast and pytorch3d: usually 30 to 90 minutes, needs network and a few GB of disk. Reopen Studio afterwards.

scene.splits.range_hint: First and last frame of the split, inclusive (0 to {last}). Default: the whole scene. A short range makes trial runs faster.
viewer.field.camera_hint: Poses and field of view of the recording cameras, in the scene's coordinate frame. The scene opens at the video's viewpoint; with follow on, the view tracks the camera while playing, interpolated between frames for smooth motion (pause on a frame for the camera's exact view).
viewer.camera.path_hint: Free: the camera stays put, move it with the mouse. Original camera: follows the selected real camera, like the full_set video. Novel path: follows a new path through 5 front-camera poses, smoothly interpolated, like the novel/front_center_interp video; these views were never captured, so there is no real image to compare.

run.colab.hint: The job runs on the Colab VM detached from this connection: closing Studio or losing the network does not stop it. Studio pulls the results when the job ends and stops the session when the run succeeded. If Colab reclaims the VM, everything not yet pulled is lost; push again to resume from the pulled copy.

viewer.stale.hint: This preview package was made by an older version of the tool, so it has no sky, humans or colour correction. Click to re-export it from the run's checkpoint (the run must be fully pulled); the scene reloads when it is done.
viewer.stale.timeout: not done after 10 minutes; see the run page for the error
lens.hint: The scene only records the lens type of each camera. A split picks which cameras are used for training; the approach's renderer must be able to draw every camera of the split.
scene.splits.lens_fisheye: This split has fisheye cameras: only the 3DGUT and 3DGEER renderers can draw them (3DGS draws pinhole only).
scene.splits.lens_pinhole: This split has pinhole cameras only: every renderer can draw it.
new.camera.make_pinhole: The chosen split has fisheye cameras, so the 3DGS renderer is locked. To use 3DGS, create a split with pinhole cameras only on the scene page
run.stages.breakdown: Of which: training {train} · start-up, data loading, checkpoints {other} · evaluation and video rendering {eval}
run.stages.breakdown_old: Of which: training {train} · the rest (start-up, checkpoints, evaluation, video rendering) {other}
run.stages.eval_reads_hint: The actual evaluation (test renders, metrics, videos) runs at the end of the train stage and is counted in that stage's time. This stage only reads the results, so it takes almost no time.
run.stages.vram_unknown: Not measured: this stage runs the GPU in a separate process and does not report VRAM, or it does not use the GPU.
densify.short.default: {rule}: from step {start}, every {every} steps, threshold {thresh} ({statistic}), splitting stops at step {stop}
densify.rule_help.default: DriveStudio's rule: Gaussians whose average position gradient exceeds the threshold are cloned (small) or split (large); faint or oversized Gaussians are culled; opacity is reset periodically.
densify.rule_help.fastgs: Same schedule as the default rule, but FastGS only splits or clones Gaussians that contribute to high-error image regions and culls more error-causing Gaussians (docs/methods/fastgs.md).
densify.rule_help.mcmc: A fixed Gaussian budget per node: near-transparent Gaussians move to opaque ones, new ones are added up to the cap, and positions get noise (docs/methods/densify_mcmc.md). Removed from the options after scoring lower than the default rule.
densify.key.stop_split_at: Stop cloning and splitting at step
densify.mcmc.grow_rate: Added per step (fraction of current count)
densify.mcmc.min_opacity: Relocate Gaussians with opacity up to
densify.source: Read from the train stage's config.yaml (command-line overrides included).
viewer.field.fov_hint: Focal length of the browser's pinhole camera (experimental), in pixels of the selected camera's training image size (the unit of K in cameras.json; KITTI-360 image_02: 700×700, source focal length 208 px), with the matching vertical field of view: f = (height / 2) / tan(angle / 2). A long focal length is a narrow view (zoomed in), a short one a wide view. With "Use the source camera's focal length" checked, the browser uses the selected camera's focal length and principal point (K), as before the slider existed: a pinhole camera then matches the source image and the video, while a fisheye camera (KITTI-360 image_02, image_03) gives about 119° with stretched edges, because the browser can only draw pinhole. Uncheck it or drag the slider for a pinhole camera with your own focal length, centred principal point, same position and direction. The range is the same for every camera: 10° to 170° vertical field of view. The exact image overlay uses the same focal length.
viewer.fov.native: Use the source camera's focal length
viewer.hud.fps_hint: Frames the browser drew in the last second. The viewer only redraws when the view changes (camera moves, playback), so there is no FPS while idle.
video.no_layout: These videos have no camera layout file, so only the tiled frame can be shown. Create it with: python -m drive2sim.scripts.video_layouts <run_id>
video.missing: This run has no {channels}. Runs trained before 20/11/2026 did not write these videos.
video.keys: Keys: space plays or pauses, ← → step one frame (click the player first). Drag on the image to move the slider.
scene.rig.diagram_caption: The vehicle faces up. Wedges show each camera's horizontal field of view (teal: pinhole, orange: fisheye); the body outline is estimated from the camera positions, not the real size.
scene.rig.trajectory_caption: Hollow circle: first frame; square: last frame; orange dot and line: vehicle position and heading at the selected frame. Distance {length} m, height change {climb} m.
scene.rig.none_hint: The scene was ingested before this feature. Creating it needs PyTorch (Studio started from the drive2sim environment) and takes a few dozen seconds.
scene.rig.forward_motion: Vehicle heading taken from the driving direction
scene.rig.forward_camera: The vehicle does not move: heading taken from where {camera} looks
scene.rig.source_hint: Poses come from the same loader the trainer uses (reports/rig.json, drive2sim/recon/tools/scene_rig.py), so the layout matches the training data. Heading is measured from the angle between the driven path and a camera's view over the whole scene, to about 2 degrees. Fisheye field of view is the part of the image where the lens model is valid; training with 3DGUT or 3DGEER also masks beyond 88 degrees per side.
figure.svg_hint: SVG: stays sharp when scaled, works in LaTeX and Word
scene.egomask.title: Ego-vehicle mask
scene.egomask.hint: Image area covered by the ego vehicle (hood, mirror, door). The body is rigid with the camera, so one mask per camera serves every frame. Masked pixels are left out of the loss, the metrics and the LiDAR projection. Masks live in the scene's ego_masks/<camera>.png; datasets that ship masks get them copied there by the converter.
scene.egomask.how_to: This image is the median of multiple frames: moving scenery is blurred while the vehicle body stays visible. Left-click to add green points on the body to mask; right-click to add red points on areas to keep. SAM2.1 updates the mask after each click. Save when the result is correct.
scene.egomask.no_sam2: SAM2.1 is not installed, so masks cannot be segmented ({hint}). Saved masks can still be viewed and deleted.
scene.egomask.none: This camera has no mask: every pixel is used.
scene.egomask.draft: Draft mask covers {coverage} of the image, not saved.
scene.egomask.saved: Saved mask covers {coverage} of the image.
scene.egomask.pending: {count}/{total} cameras still undecided: draw a mask if the camera sees the ego vehicle, or click "No ego body". Training still runs, but a visible ego body gets baked into the scene.
scene.egomask.all_done: Every camera has a mask or is confirmed to see no ego body.
scene.egomask.from_tool: Uses the mask shipped with the tool for this dataset (drawing a new mask replaces it).
scene.egomask.from_dataset: The dataset ships per-frame masks (for example PhysicalAI invalid_masks/).
scene.egomask.is_none: Confirmed: this camera sees no part of the ego vehicle.
scene.egomask.mark_none_hint: Confirm this camera sees no part of the vehicle; any drawn mask is deleted.
scene.lidar.title: LiDAR on images
scene.lidar.hint: LiDAR points (coloured by depth: red near, blue far) drawn on the camera images with the same projection as training. With correct calibration they sit on objects (cars, poles, wall edges); otherwise they slide off. The report warns about large errors automatically (a camera with almost no points, implausible depth, an unusually tilted camera). Offsets of a few pixels and two cameras with swapped calibration only show in the images. Not an approval step.
scene.lidar.none_hint: The scene was ingested before this feature. Needs PyTorch, takes a few seconds.
scene.lidar.none_kaggle: The scene was ingested on Kaggle before this feature; ingest again so the notebook projects LiDAR.
scene.lidar.no_images: Scene ingested on Kaggle: only the numbers are on this machine, the overlay images are in the ingest notebook's output.
scene.lidar.how_to_read: Click an image to open it full size. Check that points sit on the edges of cars, poles, walls and lane markings; points drifting off objects or lying in the sky mean wrong calibration or pose.

new.kind.per_scene.hint: Trains a new model for each scene from its own images. Slower; usually the best quality on that scene.
new.kind.feed_forward.hint: A pretrained model reconstructs the scene in one pass, with no per-scene training.
new.kind.slam.hint: Estimates the camera poses and builds the map together. Pinhole cameras only, at least two (a stereo pair).
benchmark.page.title: Benchmark
benchmark.page.lede: Ranks the finished runs of each group (track, cell, scene, split) of a benchmarks/<name>.yaml file. Ordered by Avg; a run within the tie threshold of the best is tied, and ties are settled in turn by PSNR after colour matching on the test-only camera (R2), the PSNR of the static-background .ply (R3), and train time when on the same GPU. Depth (R4), cost per 100 m (R6) and bad segments (R7) are reported alongside and never change the order. Reads the runs' result files only, no GPU; – means not measured.
benchmark.empty.title: No benchmark file yet
benchmark.empty.text: Create benchmarks/<name>.yaml in the working directory (format in CONTRACTS section 6.5) listing the run groups to rank; or see the sample data with make demo.
benchmark.group.info: A run within the tie threshold (PSNR) of the run with the best Avg is tied (≈). Among tied runs: R2, then R3, then train time (same GPU only). A step missing a value for any tied run is skipped for the whole group.
benchmark.decided.r2: R2: PSNR after colour matching on the test-only camera
benchmark.decided.r3: R3: higher PSNR of the static-background .ply
benchmark.tied: Tied with the best run (PSNR gap below the tie threshold)
benchmark.not_applicable: Not applicable: the method cannot export a static-background .ply
benchmark.not_static: The .ply is the raw state of a time-varying model (PVG, DeformableGS), not the trained static background; R3 does not break ties
benchmark.hint.psnr: PSNR on the test images of the cameras that were trained on (R1).
benchmark.hint.avg: Mip-NeRF's combined Avg metric; lower is better. Used for ranking.
benchmark.hint.camera_group: Mean PSNR per camera type, trained cameras only (a reporting dimension).
benchmark.hint.r2: R2: PSNR after an affine colour fit on the test-only camera (never trained). First tie-break.
benchmark.hint.r3: R3: PSNR of the static-background .ply render on the static region (dB); higher is better. Second tie-break; the export gap (original render minus .ply render) is in the tooltip. n/a: the method cannot export a .ply. †: the .ply is not the trained static background (PVG, DeformableGS), so R3 does not break ties.
benchmark.hint.depth: R4: AbsRel of rendered depth against LiDAR; lower is better. Reported alongside.
benchmark.hint.segments: R7: runs of 5 or more consecutive test frames, each more than 2 dB below the median; computed per camera group, test-only cameras left out. Diagnostic, not ranked.
benchmark.hint.per_100m: R6: divided by distance / 100 m; track B only.
benchmark.hint.ate: ATE as reported by the method itself (metres); not recomputed.
benchmark.hint.train: Actual train time. Only comparable between runs on the same GPU.
downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.help: Save files to the computer running the browser (also over Tailscale). Running the scene in CARLA needs scene.usdz (OpenDRIVE map, trajectory, cameras, vehicles and people) and the NuRec PLY for the Gaussian render server. The Gaussian PLY (standard 3DGS) opens in other viewers such as SuperSplat.
downloads.usdz_missing: No scene.usdz for CARLA yet: use "Run in CARLA" or open the Drive page once to build it.
drive_push.help: Push files to Google Drive through a Colab CPU session with Drive mounted (same as pulling data from Drive): connect Drive, pick files and a MyDrive folder, then Push. Files go in 32 MiB parts with MD5 checks; cancel and retry in Activity to continue, files already on Drive are skipped. File names get the last 4 characters of the run ID. Stop the session afterwards so Drive finishes syncing and no compute units are spent.
drive_push.done: Pushed to {path}. Stop the session so Drive finishes syncing and the VM is released.
drive_push.mounted: Drive is connected to this session.
drive_push.stop_help: Flush Drive buffers on the VM, unmount Drive, then stop the Colab session
